## Setup

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = next(
    p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "src").is_dir()
)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from loaders import sysco_fy26, fy26_vendor_tabs
from protein_classifier import classify_frame
from summaries import vendor_scope, class_crosstab, items, plant_share

DATA = ROOT / "data" / "raw" / "FY26"
WORKBOOK = DATA / "Food_2026_final.xlsx"
RAW_SYSCO = DATA / "Vendor Data" / "Sysco_FY26.xlsx"

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
pd.set_option("display.float_format", "{:,.2f}".format)
```

## Load the Sysco tab

Standard table; drops header and zero-dollar rows.

```{python}
sysco = sysco_fy26.load(WORKBOOK)
pd.Series(sysco.attrs["cleaning_log"], name="rows").to_frame()
```

```{python}
print(f"Lines: {len(sysco):,}  "

sysco.head()
```

## Reconcile with the raw Sysco export

Per-hall totals vs. Sysco's account totals.

```{python}
raw_totals = sysco_fy26.load_raw_totals(RAW_SYSCO)
recon = sysco_fy26.reconcile(sysco, raw_totals)
located = recon.drop(index=["(no hall)", "TOTAL"])
assert (located["usd_diff"].abs() < 0.005).all()
recon
```

## Scope

```{python}
others = fy26_vendor_tabs.load(WORKBOOK)
scope = vendor_scope(pd.concat([sysco, others]))

def k(vendor, col="usd"):
    return f"${scope.loc[vendor, col] / 1e3:,.0f}k"


s = {
    "sysco": f"{scope.loc['Sysco', 'share']:.0%}",
    "kikka": k("Kikka"),
    "newport": k("Newport Meat Company"),
    "fishking": k("Fish King Inc."),
    "wismettac": k("Wismettac Asian Foods", "Red Meat"),
    "natures": k("Nature's Produce", "Dairy/Eggs"),
}
scope[scope[["Red Meat", "Poultry", "Seafood", "Dairy/Eggs"]].sum(axis=1) > 0]
```

Sysco is `{python} s["sysco"]` of FY26 food-vendor spend. Other vendors with
protein: Kikka (`{python} s["kikka"]`, coded Seafood), Newport Meat
(`{python} s["newport"]`), Fish King (`{python} s["fishking"]`), Wismettac
(`{python} s["wismettac"]` Red Meat) and Nature's Produce
(`{python} s["natures"]` Dairy/Eggs). Their protein is mostly animal, so the
Sysco share is likely an upper bound on Pomona's overall share.

## Classify protein (draft rules)

Ordered regex rules on (description, category); first match wins.

```{python}
cls = classify_frame(sysco)
assert len(cls) == len(sysco)
```

### Plant share by definition

A: flesh vs analog + legume/soy; B: + egg vs + nut/seed; C: + dairy vs +
plant dairy alt; D: + mixed animal vs + mixed plant.

```{python}
shares = plant_share(cls)
shares.assign(
    plant_usd=shares["plant_usd"].map("${:,.0f}".format),
    animal_usd=shares["animal_usd"].map("${:,.0f}".format),
    plant_share_usd=shares["plant_share_usd"].map("{:.1%}".format),
    plant_share_lb=shares["plant_share_lb"].map("{:.1%}".format),
)
```

### Category × class, dollars

```{python}
class_crosstab(cls).round(0)
```

### Lines and dollars per rule

```{python}
cls.groupby("rule")["usd"].agg(lines="size", usd="sum").round(0)
```

### Borderline items

```{python}
borderline = (
    cls["desc"].str.contains(r"COCONUT|CHEESE CREAM|CREAM CHEESE", na=False)
    | cls["protein_class"].isin(["mixed_animal", "mixed_plant"])
)
items(cls, borderline).round(0)
```
